title: Minimum Substring Partition of Equal Character Frequency
summary: Given a string s, determine the least number of balanced substrings into which it can be divided.
statement: Given a string s, determine the least number of balanced substrings into which it can be divided. A balanced substring is one where all characters occur an equal number of times. Valid partitions include ("abab", "c", "c"), ("ab", "abc", "c"), and ("ababcc"). Invalid partitions are ("a", "bab", "cc"), ("aba", "bc", "c"), and ("ab", "abcc"), as they contain unbalanced substrings.
constraints: s is a nonempty lowercase string.
A substring is balanced when every distinct character appearing in it has the same positive frequency.
Partition all characters into the fewest nonempty balanced contiguous substrings.
hints: A partition decision depends only on its next start index; every balanced prefix is a valid next edge.
Use suffix DP and enumerate end positions while maintaining character counts.
At start i, extend j; when all positive counts are equal, minimize 1+dp[j+1].
Every valid partition begins with one enumerated balanced prefix, and optimal suffix reuse gives the minimum number of parts.
editorial: Every valid partition begins with one enumerated balanced prefix, and optimal suffix reuse gives the minimum number of parts.

tests.explanation: One optimal partition is fab, ccdd, g, so the minimum is three.
All three present characters occur twice, so the whole string is one balanced part.
